METHOD (CLAUDE.md). Three laws paid for in one session. SUFFICIENT IS NOT
ULTIMATE: a fix that works is not thereby the form, and sufficiency is the
ultimate form's most convincing costume because it passes every test you
thought to run. THE SURROUNDING CODE IS NOT A PREMISE: an "ultimate given X"
where X is unverified is X's drift laundered through your judgment — the
ultimate form of a compensation is its deletion. HARDEST FIRST: the easy
piece is easy because it assumes the hard one's answer, so building it first
means building it twice. And interrogate the ARTIFACT as hard as the prose —
compensations look like competent code, and their comments routinely name
the defect they exist to paper over ("the parser cannot see seams", "the
freeze exists so readers never read live"). Read the comment as a confession.

mentl/63a8cf1:
Substrate bug in seed's parse_binop: the right-side recursion at the operator
boundary used `pos + 1` (just past the operator token) without skipping
whitespace. When the operator is followed by a newline (`x > 0 && \n y > 0
&& \n z > 0`), parse_primary at pos+1 sees TNewline, falls through to its
LitUnit fallback (line 383-388), and returns LitUnit with pos advanced by 1.

Result: only the FIRST operand of the chain parses; the rest leaks as
orphan top-level tokens. Lowered form `(x > 0) && unit` evaluates to 0.

Symptom cascade (unmasked four substrate gates today):
  - block-int / if / match / nested-fn all produced 0B m3 output
  - The "buggy match-arm-body" was actually the second arm being misparsed
    as PVar binding from the orphaned `helper(name) >= 65 && ...`
  - SYNTAX.md §1126 (operator precedence) doesn't make newlines binop
    terminators; the parser's pos+1 was mechanically wrong

Fix: parse_binop wraps `pos + 1` in `$skip_ws_p` before recursing for
the right operand. Whitespace between operator and right-operand is
transparent per SYNTAX.md.

Empirical post-fix:
  - `fn check(name) = name > 0 && \n helper(name) >= 65 && \n helper(name) <= 90`
    compiles to the canonical full && chain WAT, identical to single-line
    form.
  - block-int: 1622B (was 1622B — unchanged, blocks were already working)
  - if: 690B (was 0)
  - match: 1668B (was 0)
  - nested-fn: 690B (was 0)
  - Full wheel self-compile: exit 0, 1141B m3 (still wheel-emit cascade
    territory, but no trap)

ROADMAP.md item 2 — SchemeKind canonicalization. src/infer.nx already
referenced CapabilityScheme(effs) at the env_extend site for
CapabilityDeclStmt and at the expand_capabilities expansion site, but
src/types.nx defined only four variants (FnScheme, ConstructorScheme,

Capability bundles are a real fifth construction origin: a capability
declaration stores a (EffName, Bool) list under a name, and effect-row
build time expands the bundle's contents inline. Re-expressing this
through the existing four variants would have been drift mode 6
(primitive-type-special-case) — capabilities are peer to functions,
constructors, effect ops, and records, not a flag on one of them.
